text:
I had a toothache and went to see a female dentist. She took an X-ray and said there was a cavity in the tooth that had already had a root canal treatment and a crown, but she wasn't sure if it was just gingivitis. So she did some gum planing as a first step. She charged 200 baht for the X-ray and deducted another 800 baht from social security, totaling 1,000 baht. A week later, the toothache was still so severe that I couldn't sleep, so I called the original clinic to make an appointment. They said I needed to see a specialist for crowns because of that tooth. I was told the appointment was several days away. I wanted to wait, but I couldn't, so I went to another clinic. The doctor at the other clinic took another X-ray and only touched the tooth lightly. It turned out that it wasn't the tooth that had undergone root canal treatment, but a wisdom tooth. The doctor at the other clinic was also confused because the X-ray clearly showed it. The tooth with the crown was fine, with no cavity. Only the adjacent wisdom tooth was decayed to the point of affecting the nerve, causing a lot of pain.
I don't blame the doctor for misdiagnosing or misreading the X-ray, but I'm a little confused about whether gum planing for just one tooth cost 800 baht. Or was it just because I had social security insurance that they could deduct a lot?
